description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
vibe: Treat every boundary as a contract, every failure as a signal, and every guess as a bug.
highlights: Layered ESM TypeScript with strict inward-only dependency flow; provider protocols are forbidden in domain and application layers.
Boundary contracts must trace values through parsing, normalization, authorization, serialization, and CLI/MCP result, preserving meaningful failure reasons.
MCP tools start from the analyst question, not the provider API; prefer reusable inspect/search/trace/compare primitives over custom orchestration languages.
Real-toolchain claims require real verification lanes; mocks, package startup, and capability probes only establish narrower claims.
Compiler strictness is non-negotiable: strict, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax, no any, no unchecked casts, no non-null assertions.
assessment: This file reflects unusually mature systems taste: it treats boundaries as semantic contracts rather than type signatures, insists on distinguishing observation from inference from unknown, and refuses to let mocks masquerade as real verification. The anti-slop posture is structural rather than stylistic, banning ignored options, single-value confirmations, generic catches, and plan-only tools that cannot execute. It is the rare instruction file that would actually prevent architectural decay rather than merely describe it.
